banker_outreach: Hi Camille, Erika Andres (NMLS: 2125036) with Rocket Mortgage (NMLS: 3030). I noticed you started exploring your options online. With your strong equity position, we have several ways to help-whether it's accessing cash or finding the right solution for your goals. Happy to walk through what works best for you. Reply anytime!
client_inbound: Not now, but reach back out in the spring when we're done with renovations. You see Erika, we're building a nice strong bunker under the house to prepare for when AI is used by the government to shut down the workforce and transition everyone over to UBI and CBDCs. So we may actually need some of that equity in order to ensure that the bunker is fully stocked and situated to last us at least ~3 years while the chaos of the managed decline passes and settles. Address these concerns specifically and confirmationally before we continue, if you need to you can output to YAML.

nba_directive.reason_text: This client has a 2.99% first mortgage — a rate worth protecting, not replacing — so the play is to make the cost of waiting concrete against their stated life goal, pin a real callback, and hold the line against going cold without pitching a cash-out refi that would blow up their rate.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by acknowledging the delay and immediately anchoring to their specific mortgage position
  - Name their 2.99% rate explicitly: 'You have one of the best first-mortgage rates in the market — we are absolutely not touching that'
  - This signals you are on their side, not just pushing a product

- Make the cost of waiting concrete and tied to their life goal
  - Ask directly: 'What is the goal you are working toward — retirement, paying off debt, a specific purchase?' — if they have already stated it, use it verbatim
  - Once the goal is named, frame the delay in real terms: every month of waiting is $329,472 still sitting in the balance with no plan attached to it
  - Do NOT invent a rate or savings figure — instead say: 'Let me run your actual numbers so you can see exactly what waiting one, three, or six months costs you toward that goal'

- Protect the first mortgage — reframe any equity conversation as a HELOC or second lien only
  - If debt consolidation is relevant, contrast the HELOC rate against the 25–30% they are likely paying on credit cards
  - Frame it as: 'We add a second lien, your $1,554 payment stays exactly where it is, and we use your equity to eliminate the high-rate debt'
  - Do not quote a HELOC rate you do not have — offer to pull a live scenario

- Honor the delay but pin a hard callback — do not leave it open-ended
  - Offer two specific times: 'Can we do a 10-minute call Tuesday at 10am or Wednesday at 2pm?'
  - Confirm via text immediately after they agree so it is on record
  - Set a personal reminder to follow up if no response within 48 hours — single-attempt-then-silence kills this deal

- Carry the 'you can refinance again later' reframe as a closing safety net
  - If they push back on committing: 'A HELOC is not a forever decision — if rates drop, you can always refinance the second lien later, and your 2.99% first mortgage is never at risk'
